## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# gh-1606 rework — CI red head fixed (CRAP gate)

## Issues/Notes

- Validation CI failed on commit `a4f525bb` with exactly one root cause, reported by two
  checks:
  - **CRAP + duplication** (guards leg): `Max CRAP: 15.55 — FAIL (threshold: 12.00)` —
    `(top-level)._effectivePlatform` at `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart:54`
    (complexity 5, line coverage 25% → CRAP = 5²·(1−0.25)³ + 5 = 15.55).
  - **Quality gate**: the aggregate required check — `Quality gate FAILED: a leg is
    failure (guards)` (`R_GUARDS: failure`; every other leg success/skipped). No
    separate duplication finding: the duplication gate is `severity: warning` (soft) and
    the job log's only `##[error]` is the CRAP line.
- Root cause: the new `/provider export` clipboard writer resolves the platform with an
  if-chain (`platform` pin → `Platform.isMacOS` → `isLinux` → `isWindows`), but every
  test in `test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart` pinned `platform:` explicitly (the seam
  exists because the macOS/Windows arms are unreachable on a Linux CI runner) — so the
  host-`Platform` fallback arm never executed and only 1 of 4 executable lines was
  covered.
- No open review threads on the PR (review_state: `NONE`, 0 threads), so no code
  findings to fix beyond the gate.

## Approach

- TDD order kept: reproduced the gate failure locally first (scoped
  `dart test test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart --coverage=coverage` → lcov →
  `crap4dart analyze lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart` → identical
  `15.55 — FAIL (threshold: 12.00)`), then turned it green.
- **No production code changed.** The function is correct and its seam design is
  documented; the gap was test coverage, so the minimum fix is the missing test.
- Added `no platform pin: the host platform resolves the clipboard path` to
  `test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart`: calls `writeClipboardText` **without** the
  `platform:` pin (the uncovered fallback arm), injected runner (no real pasteboard on
  any dev host), asserts the host-dispatched executable (`pbcopy`/`xclip`/`clip` by
  `Platform.isMacOS`/`isWindows`/else) and that the credential still rides stdin.
- Verified GREEN the same way: coverage 25% → 75%, `_effectivePlatform`
  CRAP 15.55 → **5.39**, `Max CRAP: 5.39 — OK (threshold: 12.00)`.
- CI projection: the core test shards run on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, so the merged lcov sees
  the same `Platform.isLinux` arm → same 75% → same 5.39 → guards leg passes and the
  Quality gate aggregate goes green.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart` — +28 lines: one new test exercising the
  host-`Platform` platform-resolution arm of `writeClipboardText`.

## Test Coverage

- New test covers the previously-uncovered host fallback arm: on the Linux CI runner it
  executes `if (platform != null)` (false), `Platform.isMacOS` (false),
  `Platform.isLinux` (true → return) — the exact lines that produced the 25% figure.
- `dart analyze lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart` —
  no issues.
- `dart test test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart` — 7/7 pass (6 existing + 1 new).
- Full unit suite (`dart test --concurrency=4 --exclude-tags integration`) —
  **10724 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped** (exit 0). A first run of the same suite on the
  same tree showed one failure that did not reproduce in the second run (same total

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
