# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the

  /provider [name] [baseUrl] [token] | custom | aiin [--no-browser] [key [apiKey]]
                     | openrouter oauth [headless] [--no-browser]
                     | chatgpt oauth [headless] [--no-browser] | /provider copilot
                     | codemie sso [orgUrl] [--no-browser] | dial setup | kimi
                     show or switch the provider/endpoint (token optional,
                     saved to the OS secure store when available); custom is
                     a guided setup that saves the provider (api type, url,
                     key, model); aiin signs in to aiin.by — the browser
                     flow registers a sk-aiin API key automatically
                     (a pasted key works too: /provider aiin key);
                     openrouter oauth authenticates via OpenRouter
                     PKCE and stores the resulting key in the secure store;
                     kimi switches to the Kimi Code OpenAI-compatible
                     endpoint (api.kimi.com/coding/v1, key: KIMI_API_KEY);
                     chatgpt oauth offers the saved ChatGPT accounts first
                     (pick one, or add another); a new sign-in stores the
                     OAuth credentials blob in that account's own
                     secure-store slot — access tokens refresh
                     automatically and the rotated blob is re-persisted;
                     codemie sso [orgUrl] signs in to a CodeMie organization
                     via browser SSO (localhost callback) and saves it as a
                     custom provider — the session JWT rides the standard
                     OpenAI-compatible adapter; dial setup runs the guided
                     DIAL Core flow (base URL, Api key, deployment) and
                     saves the org as a dial custom provider;
                     --no-browser skips the automatic browser launch —
                     the full authorization URL always prints (also on
                     timeout), and FA_NO_BROWSER=1 or a headless/SSH
                     session skips the launch automatically
                    /provider copilot connects a GitHub Copilot account via
                    the GitHub device flow (open the shown URL, enter the
                    code; also works headless) or by pasting an existing
                    GitHub token; the account saves as a named entry
                    (copilot-<login>, individual/business/enterprise/custom
                    endpoint) with its token in the secure store under
                    FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME> (env FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID
                    overrides the device-flow client id); the short-lived
                    Copilot token refreshes automatically

# gh-1606: Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless

## Description

## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

Token-lifetime note (verified): device-flow `gho_`/`ghu_` tokens do not expire and are not refreshed (revocation is manual); only the exchanged ~30-min Copilot API token rotates, which fa re-exchanges automatically — so an exported token stays valid until revoked.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`

- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.

2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`

`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

{"path":"AGENTS.md"}

{
  "key": "gh-1606",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless",
    "description": "## Problem
fa's `copilot` provider only supports one auth path: exchange a GitHub credential via `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token`. That endpoint accepts **only OAuth tokens** (`gho_`/`ghu_` from device flow) — a fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_…`) gets **404** on exchange, and direct Copilot API calls with a raw PAT from a generic HTTP client get **400 "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"**. So users who provision a fine-grained PAT (the officially documented token type for Copilot automation) cannot use it in fa at all — while the **official GitHub Copilot CLI can**.

## Evidence (verified empirically, 2026-10-14, Copilot Business seat `copilot_for_business_seat_quota`)
- PAT on exchange: `GET https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` → **404** (any headers/UA, incl. h2, exact CLI UA, `client_id` variants).
- PAT direct on `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/models` with generic client → **400** `Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint`.
- **PAT + first-party client identity → 200 everywhere.** Adding exactly two headers makes the identical request succeed from plain curl:
  ```
  copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli
  user-agent: copilot/1.0.97 (darwin …) term/unknown
  ```
  - `GET  /models`            → 200 (48 models)
  - `POST /chat/completions`  → 200, real completion (claude-fable-5.1 answered)
- MITM of the official Copilot CLI 1.0.95/1.0.97 with `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=<fine-grained PAT>`: it **never calls the exchange** — it sends the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly to `api.business.githubcopilot.com` with those two headers. Endpoint choice: the exchange's `endpoints.api` for OAuth tokens; for a PAT the CLI picks the seat's endpoint (business/enterprise) directly.
- `ghp_` classic PATs remain unsupported by Copilot at all (unchanged).

## Why it matters for fa
- Headless/docker: a PAT is the ideal credential — stable, revocable, scope-limited, no keychain, no interactive device flow in a container. `export COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` currently **fails** in fa; with this fix it works.
- OAuth device-flow tokens stay the recommended default (they work in both paths); this adds the PAT path.

## Proposed fix
In the copilot provider (`lib/src/providers/copilot_oauth.dart` + key resolution):
1. When the credential is a fine-grained PAT (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat`): **skip the exchange entirely**; use the raw PAT as `Bearer` directly against the Copilot API base URL (config `baseUrl` / provider profile — no `endpoints.api` to learn).
2. Attach the first-party client identity on all Copilot API requests in PAT mode:
   - `copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`
   - `user-agent: copilot/<fa-version> (<os>) term/unknown`
   (These headers are harmless for the OAuth path; decide whether to also send them there for consistency.)
3. Keep the existing exchange flow for `gho_`/`ghu_`/device-flow tokens, including its proactive ~30-min token refresh (unchanged).
4. Update the connect-error hints: for `github_pat_` stop suggesting only the "Copilot Requests" permission edit; explain that PAT mode needs fa ≥ this version or the official CLI.

## Acceptance
1. Unit/integration test (mocked http): credential `github_pat_…` → no request to `copilot_internal/v2/token` is made; requests carry the PAT bearer + the two identity headers; chat completions and models flows work.
2. Live smoke against a Copilot Business seat: `/provider copilot` + pasted fine-grained PAT connects, model list loads, one completion round-trips.
3. OAuth path regression: device-flow token still exchanges, refresh-in-lead behavior preserved (existing tests green).
4. Docs (`docs/` provider page) updated: three supported credentials — device flow (recommended), `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env (OAuth token or fine-grained PAT), classic `ghp_` never supported.

## Notes / honesty
`copilot-developer-cli` is the official CLI's client identity — we present the same first-party integration id the official CLI uses, with the user's own token and seat. GitHub documents fine-grained PATs for the Copilot CLI; using the same identity from a third-party harness is a gray zone users accept knowingly (same pattern as OSS `copilot-api`/`copilot2api` mimicking `vscode-chat`).


## Related UX gap (same card): `/provider export`
There is no fa surface to reveal a stored credential (`/key` is `set|delete` only), so moving the device-flow token to a headless box needs raw `security` incantations. Add one minimal command:

- `/provider export` — copies the full token of the saved Copilot account to the **clipboard**. That's all: no printing to the transcript, no flags, no reveal ceremony. Several accounts → reuse the existing account picker. Feedback is one line: `token copied to clipboard`.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern

                    /provider copilot connects a GitHub Copilot account via

If the key isn't preloaded, read may return null spuriously? Let me check `SecureKeyCache.read` semantics. In the tests they call `cache.preload([...])`. 14. **The export picker `_pickExportCopilotAccount` looks up `config.customProviders?.find(choice)` after picking — race if registry mutated? negligible.

15. **Clipboard writer: `wl-copy` needs args?** `wl-copy` with no args reads stdin — correct. `xclip -selection clipboard` reads stdin — correct. `clip` on Windows reads stdin — correct. `pbcopy` reads stdin — correct.

16. **A real issue candidate: `writeClipboardText` catches `on Object` and falls through silently** — if `xclip` exists but fails because no X display, falls to wl-copy, then reports generic unavailable. Fine.

17. **Deadlock risk revisited**: `process.stdin.write` + `flush` before draining stdout/stderr — with `wl-copy` on Wayland, wl-copy forks and the parent... hmm, wl-copy exits after fork? Actually `wl-copy` forks to background by default (unless `--foreground`), the parent exits immediately! That means `process.exitCode` completes quickly, and the forked child holds the clipboard content. But wait — wl-copy forks and the PARENT exits — does the parent read stdin fully before forking? wl-copy reads all of stdin, then forks. OK fine.

But `xclip` by default forks into background too (unless `-f`/verbose)! Actually xclip daemonizes when selection is set... xclip: "xclip forks unless -f is given". The forked xclip child serves the selection later. The parent exits after reading stdin. So exit code 0 arrives. The credential rides in the forked child's memory serving the clipboard. Fine behavior-wise.

18. **More important: `/provider export` with FA_KEY env**: In CI/store-less mode, keys resolve from `FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env. `config.secureKeys` — is that the SecureKeyCache which also resolves env? The export reads only `config.secureKeys?.read(keyName)` — if the user runs store-less with env var, is the token visible via export? SecureKeyCache presumably includes env? Let me check `SecureKeyCache.read`.

Per AGENTS.md: "DEFAULT endpoint resolves env → `FA_KEY_<HOST>` → ...". The env fallback happens at provider key resolution (in bin/fah.dart `_resolveApiKey` via `optionalProviderApiKey`), NOT in SecureKeyCache. So `/provider export` on a store-less CI box with `FA_KEY_COPILOT_X` env set would say "no stored token" — because the token rides the env, not the secure store snapshot. Is that a gap? `SecureKeyCache.read(name)` is a synchronous snapshot read. The snapshot is populated at boot `preload(names)` — which names does the CLI preload at boot? If the CLI preloads all `FA_KEY_*` names referenced by config, then a copilot entry's keyName is preloaded. When a NEW copilot account is connected during the session, `save()` writes through to the snapshot. So the export path reads the snapshot — fine for entries connected in-session or preloaded at boot.

But: what about keys resolved from ENV (`FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env)? Docs say "CI runs store-less via the `FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME>` env". Where does the env → key resolution happen? Per AGENTS.md: "DEFAULT endpoint resolves env → `FA_KEY_<HOST>` → ...". The env fallback happens at provider key resolution (in bin/fah.dart `_resolveApiKey` via `optionalProviderApiKey`), NOT in SecureKeyCache. So `/provider export` on a store-less CI box with `FA_KEY_COPILOT_X` env set would say "no stored token" — because the token rides the env, not the secure store snapshot. Is that a gap? The export targets "moving the device-flow token to a headless box" — the token is IN the store on the source machine, so export works there. On the CI box you don't need export. So acceptable. But does the secure store snapshot include env-provided keys? Let me check how SecureKeyCache is preloaded — maybe env keys get seeded into the cache too. Let me check bin/fah_runapp.dart for preload calls and env seeding.

Actually let me check where preload is called with what names, and whether env keys are seeded into the cache.

One subtle issue: in PAT mode, if `_fetchProviderModelIds` returns an empty list for ANY reason (dead network, timeout, JSON parse error), the CLI says "the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — check the Copilot Requests permission..." — a misleading hint when the actual cause was a network error. The dialect swallows all errors into an empty tuple. So the message conflates "PAT rejected" with "network down". Minor (suggestion) — but for a PAT user, the new note is printed even when e.g. the API 500s. Could matter for support burden but is a UX nit. Hmm — but the pre-existing behavior for OAuth had the same issue (exchange warning shown, then silent empty). The new message actively names wrong causes on transient errors. I'd file as SUGGESTION.

Now `_applyCopilotCredentials` — after PAT connect, the saved entry is a custom provider entry with apiType 'copilot'. At runtime, how does the provider resolution work for a copilot entry? `providerKind: 'copilot'` → streamCopilot with githubToken resolved from the key slot. The runtime path: `_resolveApiKey('copilot', keys, baseUrl: ...)` — env first (FA_KEY_COPILOT...), then store. In PAT mode the raw PAT becomes the bearer. OK.

PAT format is `github_pat_<22 chars>_<59 chars>` — alphanumeric+underscore only, so `.` can't appear; proxy host needs dots. The regex is `proxy-ep=([^;]+)` — requires a `;` before the value? One subtle issue: in PAT mode, if `_fetchProviderModelIds` returns an empty list for ANY reason (dead network, timeout, JSON parse error), the CLI says "the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — check the Copilot Requests permission..." — a misleading hint when the actual cause was a network error. The dialect swallows all errors into an empty tuple. So the message conflates "PAT rejected" with "network down". PAT format is `github_pat_<22 chars>_<59 chars>` — alphanumeric+underscore only, so `.` can't appear; proxy host needs dots. The regex is `proxy-ep=([^;]+)` — requires a `;` before the value? No — the regex is `proxy-ep=([^;]+)` and `firstMatch` — it doesn't require a preceding `;`. The PAT charset is `[A-Za-z0-9_]` — no `=`, no `.`. So no injection. Fine.

One subtle issue: in PAT mode, if `_fetchProviderModelIds` returns an empty list for ANY reason (dead network, timeout, JSON parse error), the CLI says "the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — check the Copilot Requests permission..." — a misleading hint when the actual cause was a network error. The dialect swallows all errors into an empty tuple. So the message conflates "PAT rejected" with "network down". back to the main connection)
  /model-edit [contextWindow|maxTokens <n>]
                     show or override the active model's token limits for
                     this session (an endpoint-reported window from /models
                     wins over the 200k catalog default; persist per chain
                     via roles yaml contextWindow:/maxTokens:)
  /provider [name] [baseUrl] [token] | custom | aiin [--no-browser] [key [apiKey]]
                     | openrouter oauth [headless] [--no-browser]
                     | chatgpt oauth [headless] [--no-browser] | /provider copilot
                     | codemie sso [orgUrl] [--no-browser] | dial setup | kimi
                     show or switch the provider/endpoint (token optional,
                     saved to the OS secure store when available); custom is
                     a guided setup that saves the provider (api type, url,
                     key, model); aiin signs in to aiin.by — the browser
                     flow registers a sk-aiin API key automatically
                     (a pasted key works too: /provider aiin key);
                     openrouter oauth authenticates via OpenRouter
                     PKCE and stores the resulting key in the secure store;
                     kimi switches to the Kimi Code OpenAI-compatible
                     endpoint (api.kimi.com/coding/v1, key: KIMI_API_KEY);
                     chatgpt oauth offers the saved ChatGPT accounts first
                     (pick one, or add another); a new sign-in stores the
                     OAuth credentials blob in that account's own
                     secure-store slot — access tokens refresh
                     automatically and the rotated blob is re-persisted;
                     codemie sso [orgUrl] signs in to a CodeMie organization
                     via browser SSO (localhost callback) and saves it as a
                     custom provider — the session JWT rides the standard
                     OpenAI-compatible adapter; dial setup runs the guided
                     DIAL Core flow (base URL, Api key, deployment) and
                     saves the org as a dial custom provider;
                     --no-browser skips the automatic browser launch —
                     the full authorization URL always prints (also on
                     timeout), and FA_NO_BROWSER=1 or a headless/SSH
                     session skips the launch automatically
                    /provider copilot connects a GitHub Copilot account via
                    the GitHub device flow (open the shown URL, enter the
                    code; also works headless) or by pasting an existing
                    GitHub token; the account saves as a named entry
                    (copilot-<login>, individual/business/enterprise/custom
                    endpoint) with its token in the secure store under
                    FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME> (env FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID
                    overrides the device-flow client id); the short-lived

back to the main connection)
  /model-edit [contextWindow|maxTokens <n>]
                     show or override the active model's token limits for
                     this session (an endpoint-reported window from /models
                     wins over the 200k catalog default; persist per chain
                     via roles yaml contextWindow:/maxTokens:)
  /provider [name] [baseUrl] [token] | custom | aiin [--no-browser] [key [apiKey]]
                     | openrouter oauth [headless] [--no-browser]
                     | chatgpt oauth [headless] [--no-browser] | /provider copilot
                     | codemie sso [orgUrl] [--no-browser] | dial setup | kimi
                     show or switch the provider/endpoint (token optional,
                     saved to the OS secure store when available); custom is
                     a guided setup that saves the provider (api type, url,
                     key, model); aiin signs in to aiin.by — the browser
                     flow registers a sk-aiin API key automatically
                     (a pasted key works too: /provider aiin key);
                     openrouter oauth authenticates via OpenRouter
                     PKCE and stores the resulting key in the secure store;
                     kimi switches to the Kimi Code OpenAI-compatible
                     endpoint (api.kimi.com/coding/v1, key: KIMI_API_KEY);
                     chatgpt oauth offers the saved ChatGPT accounts first
                     (pick one, or add another); a new sign-in stores the
                     OAuth credentials blob in that account's own
                     secure-store slot — access tokens refresh
                     automatically and the rotated blob is re-persisted;
                     codemie sso [orgUrl] signs in to a CodeMie organization
                     via browser SSO (localhost callback) and saves it as a
                     custom provider — the session JWT rides the standard
                     OpenAI-compatible adapter; dial setup runs the guided
                     DIAL Core flow (base URL, Api key, deployment) and
                     saves the org as a dial custom provider;
                     --no-browser skips the automatic browser launch —
                     the full authorization URL always prints (also on
                     timeout), and FA_NO_BROWSER=1 or a headless/SSH
                     session skips the launch automatically
                    /provider copilot connects a GitHub Copilot account via
                    the GitHub device flow (open the shown URL, enter the
                    code; also works headless) or by pasting an existing
                    GitHub token; the account saves as a named entry
                    (copilot-<login>, individual/business/enterprise/custom
                    endpoint) with its token in the secure store under
                    FA_KEY_COPILOT_<NAME> (env FA_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID

                     chatgpt oauth offers the saved ChatGPT accounts first

                     secure-store slot — access tokens refresh

                     codemie sso [orgUrl] signs in to a CodeMie organization

arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

`packages/fa_llm` is a separate Dart package with its OWN copilot implementation (copilot_provider.dart, copilot_token.dart, copilot_token_manager.dart...). This is the package the Flutter app uses (`fa_llm`). The PR did NOT touch `packages/fa_llm` — so the app-side copilot provider may still be the old exchange-only path!

Wait — but flutter_app/lib/services/copilot_connect_flow.dart imports `package:flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness.dart` for `fetchModelsForEndpoint` and uses fa_llm's `requestCopilotDeviceCode` / `pollCopilotAccessToken` / `fetchGithubLogin`. import subprocess, re, json
diff = subprocess.run(['git','--no-pager','diff','origin/main...HEAD'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
added, ctx = {}, {}
cur = None; newline = None
for line in diff.splitlines():
    if line.startswith('diff --git'):
        cur = line.split(' b/')[-1]; added.setdefault(cur,set()); ctx.setdefault(cur,set())
    elif line.startswith('@@') and cur:
        newline = int(re.search(r'\+(\d+)', line).group(1))
    elif cur and newline is not None:
        if line.startswith('+'): added[cur].add(newline); newline += 1
        elif line.startswith('-'): pass
        else: ctx[cur].add(newline); newline += 1
d = json.load(open('outputs/pr_review.json'))
ok = True
for c in d['inlineComments']:
    p, n = c['path'], c['line']
    mark = 'ADDED' if n in added.get(p,set()) else ('CONTEXT' if n in ctx.get(p,set()) else 'OUTSIDE')
    if mark == 'OUTSIDE': ok = False
    print(mark, f"{p}:{n}")
print('ALL ANCHORS ATTACHABLE' if ok else 'FAIL')
EOF

The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.
